plants.name: Prunus mume
plants.description: A small deciduous tree that produces fragrant five-petaled blossoms on bare branches in late winter, often while snow is still on the ground. It is widely cultivated in gardens and orchards and is prized in East Asian culture as a symbol of perseverance.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late winter to early spring (January to March)
plants.location: China, Japan, Korea; cultivated in temperate gardens worldwide
plants.funFact: Ume blossoms are celebrated at festivals in Japan, and the fruit is pickled to make umeboshi and steeped to make umeshu liqueur.

plants.name: Galanthus nivalis
plants.description: A small bulbous perennial with nodding, bell-shaped white flowers marked with green on the inner petals. It carpets woodlands and gardens, often pushing up through frost and snow.
plants.location: Europe, naturalized in the UK and North America; woodlands and gardens
plants.funFact: Snowdrops produce a compound called galantamine, which has been developed into a medicine used to treat symptoms of Alzheimer's disease.

plants.name: Hamamelis x intermedia
plants.description: A large deciduous shrub with spidery, ribbon-like petals that cluster along bare stems. The flowers are often spicily fragrant and tolerate freezing temperatures by curling up on cold days.
plants.bloomingSeason: Mid-winter to late winter (December to March)
plants.location: Temperate gardens of Europe and North America; parent species from Asia
plants.funFact: Witch hazel petals curl into tight spirals in freezing weather and unfurl again when it warms, protecting the flower from frost damage.

plants.name: Delonix regia
plants.description: A spreading tropical tree with fern-like leaves and spectacular clusters of large flowers. In parts of the Southern Hemisphere tropics, such as northern Australia, Madagascar, and parts of Brazil, it can be seen in bloom in the warm, wet season.
plants.bloomingSeason: Summer in the Southern Hemisphere (December to March); spring to summer in the north
plants.location: Native to Madagascar; widely planted in tropical and subtropical regions
plants.funFact: Despite being cultivated across the tropics, the flamboyant tree is endangered in its native Madagascar because of habitat loss.
